dedupe_keys.name: tile2net pedestrian infrastructure mapping from aerial imagery

description: Tile2Net is an end-to-end open-source tool that maps pedestrian infrastructure from aerial imagery: a semantic segmentation model detects roads, sidewalks, crosswalks and footpaths in orthorectified tiles, the results are converted to geo-referenced polygons, and a topologically interconnected centreline network is generated for pedestrian modelling. The authors present it as a low-cost way for cities on tight budgets to produce planimetric sidewalk data, and it is described in 'Mapping the walk' in Computers, Environment and Urban Systems (2023). Coverage: regions whose public high-resolution tiles are configured; the README lists additions such as Alameda County and the whole of Oregon, and users can add regions with open tiles. Access: Python code on GitHub, released as a beta with an updated API. Licence: BSD 3-Clause. Caveats: accuracy depends on imagery resolution and tree or shadow occlusion, and the beta API may change. The README notes the model also underlies an Esri pedestrian infrastructure classification model. Simulation uses: building sidewalk networks for walkability, accessibility and evacuation models where cities lack planimetric data. Related records: Project Sidewalk accessibility labels and the DC sidewalk condition assessment.
